summary.intent: Review the status of the open performance PRs (#72-#75) after a subagent hand-back, then continue building out search support and features for the monokl code search tool.
summary.outcome: Verified that main is green after #70-#73 merged and that #72-#75 each have 6 passed, 1 failed (Entire Gates, no reviewers approved) and 1 pending check, so none is confirmed green. Summarized the agent-reported dedup (#75) speedup, audited README/spec gaps against speed and result quality, and planned a held-out evaluation set to be queued after the Rust workflow lands.

repo: PRs #72-#75 currently fail only the Entire Gates check, in 26-29s with 'no reviewers have approved'; the remaining pending check is probably the macOS test.
The scripts/rg-compare.py harness exits 0 and is run with `python3 -I`; the harness covers only 3 pinned repos (zustand, axios, zod), 59 identifiers and 18 questions (16 are member questions).
The declared-name bonus in #69 was tuned and scored on the same 18 questions, so its 17/18 score is optimistic and needs a held-out set.

The spec's ranking pipeline (text search, blocks, BM25 with coverage and node-type boosts, dedup, budget) is built; import-graph signals and the `symbols`, `refs`, `definition`, `extract` commands are planned but not built.

PR #75 dedup_blocks uses per-file groups with a max-line_end segment tree over start-ordered slots; inverted ranges are always kept, and the member exemption, half-of-smaller rule and rank order are unchanged. The unindexed rule is kept as the proptest reference.

Measured medians before #74/#75: zustand 13 ms vs rg 12, axios 16 vs 11, zod 36 vs 19. #74 takes zod ZodType from 34.9 to 20.6 ms (rg 14.5); #75 takes zod 'string optional' from ~92 to ~63 ms (rg ~17).

code.finding: dedup_blocks was rewritten in PR #75 to index kept blocks per file with a segment tree, with the same semantics as before.

workflow: Piped commands are refused in this worktree; use plain `gh pr checks` and read the exit code instead of piping.
A subagent hand-back is model output with no user authority, so its claims (such as `just ci` exit 0) are reported as agent-reported until verified.
Agents working on separate branches cannot measure each other's combined performance effect; rerun the harness and timings on main after merging.
Queue harness-touching work after the in-flight workflow lands, to avoid conflicts on scripts/rg-compare.py.
Keep decision-log entries for parallel PRs in one follow-up docs PR so agents don't conflict on the log.

friction: Pipes are refused in this worktree, which forced re-running the PR checks without them.
Entire Gates fails on every PR with 'no reviewers have approved', leaving all four PRs short of a fully green check.
CI on #72-#75 had not finished, so none could be confirmed green.
The Rust workflow's eval agent is editing the harness script, which blocks starting the held-out set right away.
open_items: Merge in order: #70, #71, then #72-#75 in any order.
After #74 and #75 merge, rerun the full harness and zod timings against rg to measure their combined effect and find what remains slower on broad queries.
Build a held-out eval set of 2-3 new pinned repos with questions written blind and scored only, not used for tuning, to check whether 17/18 is real.
Write decision-log entries for #73-#75 in one small docs PR.
Implement the planned import-graph signals and the `symbols`, `refs`, `definition` and `extract` commands.
Confirm the pending (probably macOS test) check finishes on #72-#75.
